assumptions.text: The input notes will adhere to GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) as the base standard for rendering (supporting tables, task lists, etc.).
Search functionality will be implemented client-side using a pre-built index, suited for static hosting.
The target scale for the notebook is personal or small-group use (e.g., < 5,000 notes), allowing for in-browser search indexing without performance issues.
The output structure will use relative paths suitable for hosting on any generic static file server (GitHub Pages, Netlify, S3) without specific server-side mapping config.
In the absence of a specific convention, we will assume support for standard Markdown relative path links (e.g., `[text](./note.md)`) and tags defined in a YAML frontmatter `tags` list.
In the absence of a specified count, we will design for a moderate scale of up to 1,000-2,000 notes, using a lightweight client-side search library (e.g., Lunr.js, FlexSearch).
In the absence of a specified format, we will proceed with creating a command-line interface (CLI) tool, as this is common for static site generators and was listed as an acceptable assumption.
